title: Bounded-below derived smooth base change
statement:
In the square of
[sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] with $f$ smooth, $g$ quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, and $\mathcal P$ the set of primes invertible on
$S$: for $K\in D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et})$,

$$
{\operatorname{BC}}_{f,g}(K):Lf^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rh_*Le^*K
$$

in $D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(X_{\Et})$.

proof.text: Choose $a\in\mathbf Z$ with $H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$. For each integer $n$, put $K_n=\tau_{\le n}K$ and let $i_n:K_n\to K$ be the canonical map. The explicit standard truncation has $H^q(K_n)=H^q(K)$ for $q\le n$ and zero otherwise. Thus $K_n$ is bounded (zero if $n<a$) and its cohomology stalks have only prime divisors in $\mathcal P$. In particular $K_n\in D^b_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et})$.

Apply [sbc-thm-bounded-allowable-torsion] to $K_n$. The smoothness of $f$, the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $g$, and the same set $\mathcal P$ are exactly its hypotheses. Its unconditional ambient-derived-category conclusion gives that $\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}(K_n)$ is an isomorphism; no upper bound on the cohomology of its images is assumed.

Write $A=Lf^*Rg_*$ and $B=Rh_*Le^*$. By [sbc-lem-bounded-below-truncation-criterion], $H^n(A(i_n))$ and $H^n(B(i_n))$ are isomorphisms. Naturality of the exchange map at $i_n$ gives $H^n(B(i_n))\,H^n(\operatorname{BC}(K_n))=H^n(\operatorname{BC}(K))\,H^n(A(i_n))$. Therefore $H^n(\operatorname{BC}(K))=H^n(B(i_n))\,H^n(\operatorname{BC}(K_n))\,H^n(A(i_n))^{-1}$ is an isomorphism, for every integer $n$, including $n<a$.

The functors $Rg_*$ and $Rh_*$ act on bounded-below categories by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and the derived inverse images do so by [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]. Thus $A(K)$ and $B(K)$ are in $D^+(X_{\Et})$. Step 3 gives isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves, hence on all their geometric stalks. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] on $X$ to obtain the isomorphism in $D^+(X_{\Et})$.

We check the allowable-torsion typing separately. For any abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\Et}$ with $\mathcal P$-torsion stalks, let $M$ be the divisibility poset of positive integers having only prime factors in $\mathcal P$ (including $1$), and put $F[m]=\ker(m:F\to F)$. This poset is filtered, since $mm^{\prime}$ is a common upper bound. The stalk functor is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and preserves colimits: by [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk] it is inverse image to the geometric point followed by an equivalence, and inverse image is a left adjoint by [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Hence on every stalk the canonical map $\varinjlim_{m\in M}F[m]\to F$ is the union of the kernels of multiplication by $m$, which is all of the stalk by hypothesis. Conservativity of geometric stalks gives $F=\varinjlim_{m\in M}F[m]$. Since $g$ is qcqs, [lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit] now gives $R^pg_*F=\varinjlim_{m\in M}R^pg_*F[m]$ for $p\ge0$. Each term is killed by $m$: the additive derived functor sends the equality $m\operatorname{id}_{F[m]}=0$ to $m\operatorname{id}_{Rg_*F[m]}=0$, and then take $H^p$. Every element of every stalk of the displayed colimit thus is killed by some $m\in M$. Consequently $R^pg_*F$ has $\mathcal P$-torsion stalks.

proof.text: Apply the first hypercohomology filtration of [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] to the given Cartesian square, relabelling its $(X,Y,X^{\prime},Y^{\prime})$ as $(T,S,Y,X)$ and its $(f,g,f^{\prime},g^{\prime})$ as $(g,f,h,e)$, and to $K$ on $T$. Its $E_2^{p,q}=R^pg_*H^q(K)$ has $\mathcal P$-torsion stalks by step 5. Its finite filtration of $H^n(Rg_*K)$ involves only $a\le q\le n$. All later-page terms are subquotients of earlier terms. Exactness of geometric stalks therefore makes each graded stalk a subquotient of a $\mathcal P$-torsion group. Subgroups and quotients preserve the property. It also survives extensions: if the image of $x$ in the quotient is killed by $m\in M$ and $mx$ in the subobject is killed by $m^{\prime}\in M$, then $mm^{\prime}x=0$. Induct along the finite filtration. Thus every cohomology sheaf of $Rg_*K$ has $\mathcal P$-torsion stalks.

proof.text: Inverse image $f^{-1}$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] identifies $H^n(A(K))$ with $f^{-1}H^n(Rg_*K)$. For a geometric point $\bar x:P\to X$, [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk] identifies its stalk with $\Gamma(P,\bar x^{-1}f^{-1}H^n(Rg_*K))=\Gamma(P,(f\bar x)^{-1}H^n(Rg_*K))$, and hence with $H^n(Rg_*K)_{f\bar x}$. The middle identification is clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], applied with $u=f:X\to S$ and $v=\bar x:P\to X$. Step 6 makes this a $\mathcal P$-torsion group. Thus $A(K)$ lies in $D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(X_{\Et})$; its isomorphic object $B(K)$ does also, because the isomorphism induces isomorphisms on all cohomology stalks. This is a full subcategory by [sbc-def-derived-categories-with-allowable-torsion], so the ambient isomorphism and its inverse are morphisms in it, proving the claim with the corrected target site $X_{\Et}$.
